channel.title: Math paradoxes
channel.description: The Monty Hall problem, the birthday paradox and other puzzles where intuition fails. Play them, run simulations and follow clear explanations.

item.title: Survivorship bias: Wald's planes
item.description: Bombers come back with holes in the fuselage and wings, and hardly any on the engines. Where should the armour go?
item.content:encoded: Bombers come back with holes in the fuselage and wings, and hardly any on the engines. Where should the armour go?

media:content.media:description: A bomber seen from above, covered in bullet holes, with a question mark. Where should the armour go?

item.title: Braess's paradox
item.description: 4,000 drivers take 65 minutes to get to work. The city opens a free, instant shortcut between the routes. Will the trip get shorter or longer?
item.content:encoded: 4,000 drivers take 65 minutes to get to work. The city opens a free, instant shortcut between the routes. Will the trip get shorter or longer?

media:content.media:description: A road network from Start to Finish via A and B, with a new dashed shortcut A → B and a question mark. Will the new road make the trip faster?

item.title: The bridge and the torch
item.description: Four people must cross a bridge for two at night with one torch. They take 1, 2, 5 and 10 minutes. What is the least time for the whole crossing?
item.content:encoded: Four people must cross a bridge for two at night with one torch. They take 1, 2, 5 and 10 minutes. What is the least time for the whole crossing?

media:content.media:description: A night bridge over a river, four people on the bank and one torch. How many minutes until all of them are across?

item.title: 25 horses and 5 lanes
item.description: 25 horses, a track for only 5 and no stopwatch. How many races do you need to find the three fastest horses and their order for sure?
item.content:encoded: 25 horses, a track for only 5 and no stopwatch. How many races do you need to find the three fastest horses and their order for sure?

media:content.media:description: A five-lane racetrack with horses and a 5 by 5 grid beside it. How many races do you need to find the three fastest of 25 horses?

item.title: The blue-eyed islanders
item.description: A visitor tells the islanders what they already knew: "I can see someone with blue eyes." Can that change anything?
item.content:encoded: A visitor tells the islanders what they already knew: "I can see someone with blue eyes." Can that change anything?

media:content.media:description: An island where people with blue and brown eyes look at each other, and a visitor saying "I can see someone with blue eyes." What happens?

item.title: Pirates and 100 gold coins
item.description: Five logical pirates split 100 coins, and a captain whose split is not backed by half the crew goes overboard. How many coins does he keep?
item.content:encoded: Five logical pirates split 100 coins, and a captain whose split is not backed by half the crew goes overboard. How many coins does he keep?

media:content.media:description: A ship's deck, five pirates in order of rank and a chest of 100 gold coins. How many coins will the captain keep?

item.title: Hats in a line
item.description: 100 people in a line in black and white hats see only those in front of them. How many can surely name the colour of their own hat?
item.content:encoded: 100 people in a line in black and white hats see only those in front of them. How many can surely name the colour of their own hat?

media:content.media:description: A line of people in black and white hats, each seeing only the hats in front. How many of them can surely name the colour of their own hat?

item.title: Twelve coins and a balance
item.description: One of 12 coins is fake, lighter or heavier, nobody knows. How many weighings on a two-pan balance do you need to find it for sure and say which way it is off?
item.content:encoded: One of 12 coins is fake, lighter or heavier, nobody knows. How many weighings on a two-pan balance do you need to find it for sure and say which way it is off?

media:content.media:description: A two-pan balance with numbered coins on its pans. One of 12 coins is fake: how many weighings does it take to find it?

item.title: Two eggs and 100 floors
item.description: A 100-floor building and only two eggs. How many drops do you need in the worst case to find for sure the highest floor from which an egg does not break?
item.content:encoded: A 100-floor building and only two eggs. How many drops do you need in the worst case to find for sure the highest floor from which an egg does not break?

media:content.media:description: A 100-floor building with an egg falling from it. How many drops of two eggs do you need to find the highest safe floor for sure?

item.title: How many people should a poll ask
item.description: A country has 30 million voters. How many random people do you need to ask to forecast the election within ±3 points?
item.content:encoded: A country has 30 million voters. How many random people do you need to ask to forecast the election within ±3 points?

media:content.media:description: A field of voter dots, a few lit up as asked, captioned n = ?. How many people does an election poll need to ask?

item.title: The poisoned wine and the rats
item.description: One of 1,000 bottles of wine is poisoned, and the rats can test it in one round only. How many rats do you need to find the poisoned bottle for sure?
item.content:encoded: One of 1,000 bottles of wine is poisoned, and the rats can test it in one round only. How many rats do you need to find the poisoned bottle for sure?

media:content.media:description: A wine cellar with racks of bottles and rats beside them. One bottle in 1,000 is poisoned: how many rats do you need to find it?

item.title: Benford's law
item.description: Take the powers of two from 2 to 2^1000. What share of them start with the digit 1?
item.content:encoded: Take the powers of two from 2 to 2^1000. What share of them start with the digit 1?

media:content.media:description: The powers of two 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 and the nine possible first digits. Benford's law: what share of numbers start with 1?

item.title: The St. Petersburg paradox
item.description: A coin is flipped until the first tails; the pot starts at $2 and doubles with every heads. What does the game pay on average?
item.content:encoded: A coin is flipped until the first tails; the pot starts at $2 and doubles with every heads. What does the game pay on average?

media:content.media:description: A row of coins: heads double the pot, the first tails ends the game. The St. Petersburg paradox: what does this game pay on average?

item.title: The German tank problem
item.description: A factory numbers its tanks 1, 2, 3, … You come across four, numbered 4, 10, 15 and 60. How many tanks did the factory build?
item.content:encoded: A factory numbers its tanks 1, 2, 3, … You come across four, numbered 4, 10, 15 and 60. How many tanks did the factory build?

media:content.media:description: A row of tanks with factory serial numbers and four plates, 4, 10, 15 and 60, on a number line. The German tank problem: how many tanks did the factory build?

item.title: The bus paradox
item.description: A bus comes every 10 minutes on average, but with no timetable. You walk up to the stop at an arbitrary moment. How long do you wait on average?
item.content:encoded: A bus comes every 10 minutes on average, but with no timetable. You walk up to the stop at an arbitrary moment. How long do you wait on average?

media:content.media:description: A bus line with random gaps between buses and a rider at the stop. The bus paradox: how long is the average wait?

item.title: Penney's game
item.description: You pick HHH, your opponent picks THH. The coin is flipped until one of the patterns comes up in a row. What are your opponent's odds?
item.content:encoded: You pick HHH, your opponent picks THH. The coin is flipped until one of the patterns comes up in a row. What are your opponent's odds?

media:content.media:description: Coin flips, heads and tails, and two patterns, HHH and THH. Penney's game: whose pattern comes up first?

item.title: Bertrand's paradox
item.description: A chord of a circle is drawn at random. What is the chance it is longer than the side of the inscribed equilateral triangle?
item.content:encoded: A chord of a circle is drawn at random. What is the chance it is longer than the side of the inscribed equilateral triangle?

media:content.media:description: A circle with an inscribed triangle and a sheaf of random chords. Bertrand's paradox: how likely is a chord to beat the triangle's side?

item.title: Coin streaks
item.description: How long is the longest run of one side when you flip a fair coin 100 times?
item.content:encoded: How long is the longest run of one side when you flip a fair coin 100 times?

media:content.media:description: 60 coin flips, heads and tails. How long is the longest streak in 100 flips?

item.title: The two envelopes paradox
item.description: One envelope holds twice as much money as the other. You took one. Should you switch?
item.content:encoded: One envelope holds twice as much money as the other. You took one. Should you switch?

media:content.media:description: Two envelopes, one with twice as much money. The two envelopes paradox: switch or not?

item.title: Regression to the mean
item.description: After praise players do worse, and after criticism they do better. Does that mean criticism works?
item.content:encoded: After praise players do worse, and after criticism they do better. Does that mean criticism works?

media:content.media:description: A scatter plot of scores in two rounds. Regression to the mean: does praise hurt and criticism help?

item.title: How many stickers to fill an album
item.description: An album has 50 slots, and the stickers in the packs are random. On average, how many stickers do you have to buy to fill it?
item.content:encoded: An album has 50 slots, and the stickers in the packs are random. On average, how many stickers do you have to buy to fill it?

media:content.media:description: A 50-sticker album with a few empty slots left. How many stickers does it take to fill it?

item.title: The cognitive reflection test
item.description: A bat and a ball cost $1.10 together. The bat costs a dollar more than the ball. How much is the ball?
item.content:encoded: A bat and a ball cost $1.10 together. The bat costs a dollar more than the ball. How much is the ball?

media:content.media:description: A bat and a ball cost $1.10, and the bat costs $1 more. What does the ball cost?

item.title: The 100 prisoners problem
item.description: Each of 100 prisoners may open 50 of 100 boxes to find their number. All go free only if every one succeeds. What are the odds with the best strategy?
item.content:encoded: Each of 100 prisoners may open 50 of 100 boxes to find their number. All go free only if every one succeeds. What are the odds with the best strategy?

media:content.media:description: A hundred numbered boxes. The 100 prisoners problem: each may open 50 boxes.

item.title: The rope around the Earth
item.description: A rope around the equator is made 1 metre longer and lifted evenly. How big is the gap between it and the ground?
item.content:encoded: A rope around the equator is made 1 metre longer and lifted evenly. How big is the gap between it and the ground?

media:content.media:description: The Earth with a rope around it, made 1 metre longer. How high does the rope rise?

item.title: The friendship paradox
item.description: Who has more friends: you, or your friends on average?
item.content:encoded: Who has more friends: you, or your friends on average?

media:content.media:description: A friendship network with one person highlighted. The friendship paradox: who has more friends, you or your friends?

item.title: Buffon's needle
item.description: A match as long as a floorboard is wide drops onto a wooden floor at random. How often does it cross a seam between boards?
item.content:encoded: A match as long as a floorboard is wide drops onto a wooden floor at random. How often does it cross a seam between boards?

media:content.media:description: Matches on a striped board, the ones crossing a line highlighted. Buffon's needle: what are the odds of a crossing?

item.title: The two-child paradox
item.description: A family has two children, and at least one of them is a boy. What is the chance both are boys? And what if at least one of them is a boy born on a Tuesday?
item.content:encoded: A family has two children, and at least one of them is a boy. What is the chance both are boys? And what if at least one of them is a boy born on a Tuesday?

media:content.media:description: Four cards of two-child families. The two-child paradox: at least one is a boy. What is the chance both are boys?

item.title: Simpson's paradox
item.description: Treatment A beats treatment B for small kidney stones and for large ones. Can B be better for all the patients together?
item.content:encoded: Treatment A beats treatment B for small kidney stones and for large ones. Can B be better for all the patients together?

media:content.media:description: Two bars of overall treatment results: treatment A 78%, treatment B 83%. Simpson's paradox: which treatment is better?

item.title: The secretary problem
item.description: 100 candidates arrive one at a time, and you must decide on each one on the spot. What chance of hiring the best?
item.content:encoded: 100 candidates arrive one at a time, and you must decide on each one on the spot. What chance of hiring the best?

media:content.media:description: A row of 20 candidates of different quality, one highlighted. The secretary problem: how to pick the best?

item.title: The false positive paradox
item.description: 1% of people have a disease. The test is 99% accurate, and you test positive. What is the chance you're really ill?
item.content:encoded: 1% of people have a disease. The test is 99% accurate, and you test positive. What is the chance you're really ill?

media:content.media:description: A grid of 100 people, two with a positive test. The test is 99% accurate: how likely is someone really ill?

item.title: The birthday paradox
item.description: How many people must be in a room before two of them probably share a birthday?
item.content:encoded: How many people must be in a room before two of them probably share a birthday?

media:content.media:description: A birthday calendar with two people on the same day. The birthday paradox: how many people does a match take?

item.title: The duckweed lake puzzle
item.description: Duckweed doubles every day, and one plant covers a lake in 30 days. How long do two plants take?
item.content:encoded: Duckweed doubles every day, and one plant covers a lake in 30 days. How long do two plants take?

media:content.media:description: A clean lake with a few duckweed plants. One plant covers it in 30 days. What about two?

item.title: The Monty Hall problem
item.description: You're on a game show and pick one of three doors. The host, who knows where the car is, opens another door to reveal a goat and offers a switch. Should you take it?
item.content:encoded: You're on a game show and pick one of three doors. The host, who knows where the car is, opens another door to reveal a goat and offers a switch. Should you take it?

media:content.media:description: Three doors, the first one picked, a goat behind the third. The Monty Hall problem: should you switch?
